transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You said O2 is limiting because it has fewer moles, but is that the right way to decide? What should you compare instead?
I don't know. Isn't the limiting one just whichever has fewer moles?
Okay, let me think.
No, having fewer moles isn't the right way. You need to compare how much product each reactant can make.
I don't get it. How do I work out how much product each one makes?
Good question. One moment.
To find how much product each reactant makes, use the mole ratio from the balanced equation.
The mole ratio? Like the 2 and 1 in front? I still don't know what to do with them.
Let me see.
Yes, the 2 and 1 are the mole ratios. Use them to find how many moles of water each reactant can make.
Like, 3 moles of H2 makes 3 moles of water? And O2 makes... I'm not sure.
Got it. Give me a second.
Yes, 3 moles of H2 makes 3 moles of water. Now try the same for O2 using its mole ratio.
One O2 makes two water, so 2 moles O2 makes 4 moles water? So which is limiting?
Okay, let me think.
You're on the right track. Now compare how much water each reactant can make to find the limiting one.
H2 makes less, 3 moles. So H2 is limiting? Then water is 3 times 18, 54 grams?
Good question. One moment.
Yes, H2 makes less water, so it is limiting. Now calculate the mass of water from that amount.
So H2 is limiting, 3 moles water, 54 grams, not 72. Okay cool, thanks.
